rulings.challenge_claim: Two defects, raised from both sides: the closing warrant and the device note describe the recurring address tag at Jer.44.24 as adding the women beside the men, though the span's own opening verse already names them; and the unit is typed judgment_oracle and carried at high confidence over a stretch its own prose says opens with no messenger formula, with no operative-category deviation disclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both defects are real; the first needs re-cutting and the two are distinct, not one. At oshb:Jer.44.20 (byte) the tag runs עַל הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל הַנָּשִׁים֙ - the men and the women both stand there, inside an al-appositive naming who had answered. At oshb:Jer.44.24 (byte) the addressee run reads אֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל הַנָּשִׁ֑ים: the women are addressed rather than described, the preposition moves from al to el, and the men-term of oshb:Jer.44.20 does not recur at that verse at all. So the boundary prose's 'now with the women named beside the men' fails in both halves - the naming is not new, and no men-term stands at the second site. The device note is a different matter: scoped as it is to the vayomer-Yirmeyahu-el-kol-ha'am tag, the addition of all the women at oshb:Jer.44.24 (byte) is true of that tag, and what is wrong there is the gloss, which carries a conjunction the named token does not have and drops the preposition that is the actual change. The second defect verifies independently: across oshb:Jer.44.20-Jer.44.23 (byte) no messenger formula stands anywhere - the koh-amar shape first enters this movement at oshb:Jer.44.25 - and every reference to the deity is third-person, at oshb:Jer.44.21 and oshb:Jer.44.22 alike. A per-bytes type deviation is allowed with a one-sentence disclosure; the device note carries none, while the five-verse oracle at Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5 discloses its own deviation in exactly that field. The checkable defect is the missing disclosure, not the type value itself, and confidence high rests on top of it.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale, closing sentence: strike 'now with the women named beside the men' and state the byte change at oshb:Jer.44.24 instead - the addressee preposition moves from al to el and no men-term stands there - quoting that verse's addressee run at byte tier, since the claim is about its bytes and this row quotes none of them. device_notes: keep the tag-scoped recurrence claim, re-cut its gloss to the splice extent so the glossed words are the named token's own, and add the one-sentence operative-category disclosure for unit_type judgment_oracle over a span with no messenger formula and no divine first-person speech; re-set confidence from high once the type rests on a disclosed deviation. Test: read the oshb:Jer.44.20 and oshb:Jer.44.24 addressee runs side by side and check that every element the sentence names occurs where it puts it - that reading is what killed the original - and check that the type sentence names its deviation in device_notes as the Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5 unit's does.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two defects: the onset sentence's claim that the women are now named beside the men is contradicted by Jer.44.20, which already names them together, the byte change being the preposition; and the seg-layer disclosure covers only one of the three paseq-bearing verses inside the span.
rulings.grounds: Both verify, the first understates and the severity is set a step low. At oshb:Jer.44.24 (byte) the addressee run is אֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל הַנָּשִׁ֑ים: the men-term standing at oshb:Jer.44.20 (byte) in עַל הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל הַנָּשִׁים֙ does not recur at this onset at all, so 'now naming the women beside the men' fails twice - the naming is not new and the men are not there - and what the bytes change is al to el, the women moving from spoken-about to addressed. Second, the seg layer: inside Jer.44.24-Jer.44.30 four paseq segs stand over three verses - one at oshb:Jer.44.25, two at oshb:Jer.44.26, one at oshb:Jer.44.30 (single-witness, seg layer, count-only) - and the row discloses only the pair at oshb:Jer.44.26, at the one verse its argument happens to touch. Disclosure symmetry on an inventoried object is a sweep of the span, not a citation at the argued site. On severity: the onset misdescription is the same byte-false claim that closes the warrant of the unit ending at Jer.44.23, rated a full step higher there, and here it sits in the row's own onset sentence, so medium is the consistent rating. The rest of the span holds - the parashah disclosure is complete and each mark stands at its claimed type at oshb:Jer.44.24, oshb:Jer.44.25, oshb:Jer.44.29 and oshb:Jer.44.30 with the preceding oshb:Jer.44.23 cited correctly (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), no ketiv/qere note falls in the span, and the qamats-pointed divine-title reading at oshb:Jer.44.26 with its eleven-of-thirteen point-aware split is exact.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale, onset sentence: replace 'now naming the women beside the men' with the byte change at oshb:Jer.44.24 - the el-addressee widens to all the women, and no men-term stands in that verse. Same field: complete the paseq disclosure as a span sweep naming all four segs over the three verses that carry them (oshb:Jer.44.25 one, oshb:Jer.44.26 two, oshb:Jer.44.30 one), count-only, single-witness, with no intra-verse position claimed. Test: the disclosure must be re-derivable by walking every verse of the span against the seg inventory rather than the argued verse alone - the walk is what killed the original - and the onset sentence must survive reading oshb:Jer.44.20 and oshb:Jer.44.24 together.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closure warrant says the oracle closes on the neum-YHWH formula, but at Jer.45.5 that formula stands mid-verse and the life-grant clause the same sentence points to follows it.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the verse's own bytes; the two sides raise the same single defect, differing only in severity. At oshb:Jer.45.5 (byte) the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה is followed by וְנָתַתִּ֨י לְךָ֤ אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל and the verse runs on to its last word, שָֽׁם: the closing words are the life-grant to Baruch, not the formula, and the row's own splice displays the order the next clause misdescribes. Under the ruled treatment this formula is closure corroboration only, so its position is the whole of its evidential value; asserting it verse-finally where it stands mid-verse inflates the corroboration exactly at the seam that ends the parent. Medium rather than low, on a ground neither side states: this close cites no forward onset anywhere. The warrant offers the mis-positioned formula, the tier-3 mark closing oshb:Jer.45.5 (single-witness), and the chapter end, and neither the prose nor the evidence refs reach the fresh header at oshb:Jer.46.1 - so the defective claim is the only text-internal closure device the row puts on the record, and the tier-3 mark cannot carry the seam alone. The rest verifies: the whole-chapter cap posture holds at medium_low with the frontier flag set and a counted cap phrase, and the aleph-lexeme digit is right - the byte-derived device inventory lists eight verses for that lexeme with oshb:Jer.45.3 among them, matching the row's digit and object.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale, closing sentence: strike 'closing on the neum-YHWH formula' and state the position the bytes carry - the formula stands mid-verse at oshb:Jer.45.5 and the verse's last clause is the life-grant. If closure corroboration is still wanted, phrase it as the formula standing inside the closing verse and pair it with the tier-1 onset that follows at oshb:Jer.46.1, adding that ref to boundary_evidence_refs, which currently carries no forward onset citation. Test: the corrected sentence must reproduce the verse's own token order through to its last word - reading the row's own splice to the end is what killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: Three defects: the collection-scope rubric is folded into a single-nation oracle without the rubric-as-its-own-unit rival ever being tested; the address at Jer.46.11 is called the vision's first direct address although second-person imperatives already stand at 46:3 and 46:9; and the hedge withholding a count at 46:10 is attached to the bare adonai token rather than to the prefixed form actually quoted.
rulings.grounds: All three verify on bytes. Scope first: oshb:Jer.46.1 (byte) closes on עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם, plural and naming no nation, while oshb:Jer.46.2 (byte) opens לְמִצְרַ֗יִם, lamed-scoped to one. The row states that scope difference in its own prose and then carries the span to Jer.46.12, and the rival it does test is a cut after both header verses on the prose-to-poetry shift - a different seam from the one its own scope sentence raises. That rival is live under the ruled granularity, since a lamed-initial nation header is itself a tier-1 onset, and the book's opening title stands as its own superscription-typed unit at Jer.1.1-Jer.1.3; leaving it unengaged is the defect, and any actual respan is a proposal, not a finding. Second: oshb:Jer.46.3 (byte) opens עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה and oshb:Jer.46.9 (byte) opens עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙, plural imperatives rendered as commands in both witnesses, and the row's own prose calls them imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants and a summons to the allied troops. Those are direct addresses; what is new at oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) is the named vocative בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, so the defensible claim is first named vocative, and a first-claim of any kind carries a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit. Third: the form quoted at oshb:Jer.46.10 (byte) is לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת, the lamed-prefixed title stack - its own token object, byte-attested at two verses in the OAN block and invisible to a bare-token sweep. The hedge withholds a count on the ground that the bare skeleton token's point-aware split is unverified here, which is a different object; the caution is real but misfiled, and the count it declines is in fact available for the object actually quoted.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: engage the rival this row's own scope sentence raises - a cut at the oshb:Jer.46.1 / oshb:Jer.46.2 seam leaving the collection-scope rubric its own unit - and decide it on stated grounds; the rival now in the field is a different seam. Author work is to state and decide the rival in that field; moving the seam is a boundary proposal for owner adoption, never author work. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.11: replace 'The vision's first direct address' with the first named vocative, or keep a first-claim only with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.10: re-attach the hedge to the lamed-prefixed title stack actually quoted, or cite that object's own byte-attested site count instead of withholding one. Test: each cure must be re-derivable from the cited verse's own bytes for the object it names - the tests that killed the originals are reading oshb:Jer.46.3 and oshb:Jer.46.9 for imperatives before calling oshb:Jer.46.11 a first, and reading the oshb:Jer.46.10 form for its prefix before naming the sweep object.

rulings.challenge_claim: The sole ground given for rejecting the strongest rival - that the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames - is false about Jer.46.13; the class generalization backing it carries no sweep digit and is contradicted at three sites of the eleven-verse header list; and the English run for 46:18 is left without its curly delimiter.
rulings.grounds: The decisive half is upheld and the middle half needs correcting on both framing and digit. Upheld: oshb:Jer.46.13 (byte) carries its own topic clause, לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם - Nebuchadnezzar's coming to strike the land of Egypt - which is content, and is what makes the verse a topical header at all; the row quotes that very clause in its own boundary prose and then rejects the rival on the ground that the verse has no content of its own. Whatever decides that rival, this ground cannot. Correction: the class claim is that the book's other prose headers open onto their first movement rather than standing as isolated citations, and a header verse that is itself content-free and hands the movement to the next verse is not a counter-instance to that reading, so 'contradicted' overstates. What is true, and is the residual defect, is that the claim is an undigited class generalization and that the class does not behave uniformly in the respect invoked: of the eleven verses carrying the hadavar-asher-hayah header shape, four are content-free - oshb:Jer.7.1, oshb:Jer.11.1, oshb:Jer.18.1 and oshb:Jer.30.1, byte-identical eight-token headers reading הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר - and seven carry topic material. Four, not three; oshb:Jer.18.1 belongs in the count object, and a digit that names the wrong extension is itself a defect. The declared heuristic-false-positive disposition on this field's universal-claim flags does not survive: those flags land on this ground and on this generalization, and both are defects. The third item verifies in substance: the staged folded text of web:Jer.46.18 opens its second run with a curly double quote and the row's rendering substitutes a straight one, leaving that run undelimited; the run is otherwise character-for-character the staged text, so the defect is exactly the substitution, not a paraphrase.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the ground that the heading carries no content of its own - oshb:Jer.46.13's own topic clause refutes it - and decide the rival on a ground the bytes support, or re-decide it. Same field: either drop the class generalization about the book's other prose headers or give it a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; on bytes the eleven-verse header class splits four content-free against seven content-bearing, so no uniform pattern may be asserted bare. boundary_rationale, the web:Jer.46.18 run: restore the curly opening the staged folded text carries on the second run, so the run is delimited and character-exact against that text. Test: the replacement ground must survive being read against oshb:Jer.46.13's own bytes - that reading killed the original - and every WEB run in the field must pass a character-for-character comparison with the staged folded text, run by run rather than at the one cited site.

rulings.challenge_claim: The inclusio framing is overstated at the bytes: the shared element is a construct standing three times in the chapter, the same second-person address with that construct already stands at 46:11 across two row seams and undisclosed, the closing occurrence is third-person rather than the address the opening verse carries, and the framing claim carries no sweep digit.
rulings.grounds: The substance is upheld with its framing corrected: the bracket is real at the construct level and cannot bear the weight the row puts on it. A token-bound skeleton sweep of the construct returns exactly three verses, all in this chapter - oshb:Jer.46.11, oshb:Jer.46.19, oshb:Jer.46.24 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - so 'overstated' is right where 'absent' would not be. What the bytes will not carry is the framing as written. The opening edge at oshb:Jer.46.19 (byte) is a second-person address, עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ with the vocative יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם; the closing edge at oshb:Jer.46.24 (byte) reads הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה, third-person throughout. What returns at the close is therefore the construct, not the address, and the device note's gloss of both edges as one dwelling daughter fits only the opening verse - the participle stands at oshb:Jer.46.19 and nowhere at the close, so gloss extent overruns splice extent there. The third occurrence is the material one: oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) carries the same construct under the same second-person address, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י with בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, eight verses earlier and outside this span, disclosed nowhere in the row and absent from its evidence refs. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seams argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and this one runs across two of them. The front seam itself survives - the address at oshb:Jer.46.19 is genuinely fresh against the oath closing before it, and the tier-3 mark there is correctly held to corroboration - but the span-bounding force claimed for the bracket does not.
rulings.remedy: device_notes and the closing sentence of boundary_rationale: re-cut the framing claim to what the bytes bracket - the bat-Mitsrayim construct, carrying its digit and object (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - and state that the opening edge is a second-person address while the closing edge is third-person, so the bracket is on the figure and not on the address; drop the participle from the gloss of the closing edge, which does not carry it. Same fields: disclose the third occurrence at oshb:Jer.46.11, standing outside the span under the same address, and add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs. Test: the corrected framing must survive reading both edge verses for person and form, and the cohesion disclosure must come from a sweep of the construct across the chapter rather than a note at the argued edge - that sweep is what killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The couplet's cross-verse recurrence claim is left untiered where the byte tier is exact, and the English run for 46:28 is presented with no curly delimiter, with a source curly mark rendered straight inside it.
rulings.grounds: Both items verify. The recurrence is exact at the byte tier: the four-token run אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ stands identically at oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28 (byte), the sole divergence being the conjunction on the opening word - וְ֠אַתָּה at oshb:Jer.46.27 against אַ֠תָּה at oshb:Jer.46.28 (byte). The row calls that nearly verbatim with no tier named, where every recurrence claim is tier-labelled at write time and where naming the tier would strengthen this row's own cohesion argument rather than weaken it. The quote mechanics also hold: the staged folded text of web:Jer.46.28 carries a curly closing mark after the servant address, and the row's rendering substitutes a straight double quote there - a character-level divergence inside a run presented as verbatim, and the same substitution class that stands in this row's neighbourhood at web:Jer.46.18. On the missing opening delimiter the byte record refines without dissolving the point: the staged verse text itself opens mid-quote, so no opening mark was dropped; what the row still owes is a delimited run, since the mandatory curly-plus-inline-ref pairing cannot be satisfied by an opening mark the source does not supply. Low is right - neither item touches the seam, and the rest of the unit holds: the addressee shift at oshb:Jer.46.27 is a tier-1 class, the marks at oshb:Jer.46.26, oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28 each stand at their claimed type (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), the single paseq at oshb:Jer.46.28 is cited count-only, no ketiv/qere falls in the span, and the type deviation is disclosed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'nearly verbatim' with the tier-named claim - the four-token address run is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28, diverging only in the conjunction on the opening word. Same field, the web:Jer.46.28 run: restore the curly closing mark the staged folded text carries after the servant address, and give the run its own opening delimiter, since the staged verse opens mid-quote and supplies none to inherit. Test: every WEB run in the field must pass a character-for-character comparison against the staged folded text, run by run rather than at the cited site - that comparison is what killed the original - and the recurrence sentence must name the tier it collates at.

rulings.challenge_claim: The header's dating element is labelled a relative clause in two fields, but its bytes are a temporal clause, and the verse's only relative particle heads the header shape itself.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the verse's bytes. At oshb:Jer.47.1 (byte) the dating element is בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת עַזָּֽה - beterem plus a prefix-conjugation verb, a temporal subordinate clause - and the other witness renders it the same way, before Pharaoh struck Gaza. The verse's single relative particle is אֲשֶׁ֨ר, which opens the asher-hayah header shape itself, so the label both misassigns the form class and, read literally, would hand the header's own particle to the date. A form-class label is a byte-checkable claim under the same discipline as a digit, and this one is asserted twice, in the boundary prose and again in the device note, with the unit carried at high confidence and no morphology layer in the substrate to have suggested otherwise. Low is right: nothing in the seam turns on the label. The rest verifies - the header at oshb:Jer.47.1 is one of the four verses carrying that shape, the divine-speech formula at oshb:Jer.47.2 sets this frame rather than changing an established one, the marks at oshb:Jer.47.1 and oshb:Jer.47.5 stand at their claimed type with the preceding mark at oshb:Jer.46.28 cited correctly (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), the single paseq at oshb:Jer.47.2 is cited count-only, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace 'relative clause' in both fields with the byte-true class - a temporal clause on beterem plus a prefix-conjugation verb - and, if the contrast with the numbered-year date frames is kept, state it as a difference of clause type rather than of relativization. Test: the corrected label must be re-derivable from oshb:Jer.47.1's own bytes, and reading that verse for its relative particle must land on the header shape and not on the date - that reading is what killed the original.
